candidate.answerReason: The coefficient of \(x\) after combining is \(m-5\). An absent first-degree term requires this coefficient to be zero, giving \(m=5\).

methods.label: Make the first-degree coefficient zero
methods.explanation: The first-degree terms combine to give \((m-5)x\). Having no first-degree term means that its coefficient satisfies \(m-5=0\), so \(m=5\).
methods.levelReason: Uses Grade 7 coefficient cancellation and an elementary equation already within the earlier curriculum.
